stages.name: The market boys
stages.text: Boot of knock-off trainers and tick-logo tops to the market lads who'll triple it. Safe, quick, everyone believes they're the clever one. Move this lot and the day's already paid for.
stages.fail_text: Trading Standards left a friend behind last week and your buyer's got a lanyard under his coat.

stages.name: The precinct table
stages.text: Set up a folding table of boxed perfume that smells almost right. It sells while it smells, which is about an hour. More stock out means more moved before anyone's nose catches up.
stages.fail_text: A woman sprays a tester, pulls a face, and says 'fake' loud enough that the whole precinct turns round.

stages.name: The match-day holdall
stages.text: Home game, thousands walking to the ground wanting this season's shirt at a quarter of the price. A holdall empties fast on a match day — if the sponsor's printed close enough and the stewards stay lazy.
stages.fail_text: A copper on a horse clocks the badge is wrong and starts walking his horse very deliberately at your table.

stages.name: The cash-and-carry
stages.text: A back-street wholesaler buys fakes by the pallet, no questions, as long as the box says a brand. One pallet of dud razors moves in a single handshake — but pallets leave a trail a brand's lawyers can follow.
stages.fail_text: The wholesaler's had a visit from a brand-protection firm and decided the safe pallet is the one he grasses.

stages.name: The whole container
stages.text: There's a container's worth left and a bloke who 'supplies shops' who'll take the lot before teatime. Clear it all in one and you're done for a month — or you're the one holding a shipping container full of evidence.
stages.fail_text: His 'shops' are a warehouse full of officers who've been waiting for someone to offer them exactly a container.
